questions.question: The climate of India is broadly described as which type?
questions.explanation: India has a monsoon type of climate, because its weather is controlled by winds that change direction with the seasons. Polar, Mediterranean and equatorial climates belong to other parts of the world.

questions.question: The word 'monsoon' comes from the Arabic word 'mausim', which means:
questions.explanation: 'Mausim' means season. The monsoon winds are named so because they reverse their direction with the change of season; the word has nothing to do with mountains, oceans or deserts.

questions.question: Which of the following places receives the highest rainfall in India?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram in Meghalaya receives the highest rainfall in India (and the world). Jaisalmer and Leh are among the driest places, and Chennai gets only moderate rain.

questions.question: The hot and dry wind that blows over the northern plains of India during summer days is called:
questions.explanation: The loo is the hot, dry wind of the summer afternoons in north India. A blizzard is a snowstorm, a sea breeze is cool and blows on the coast, and the monsoon winds bring rain.

questions.question: In which state does the monsoon first arrive on the Indian mainland?
questions.explanation: The south-west monsoon reaches Kerala first, around the beginning of June, and then moves northwards. Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh get the monsoon several weeks later.

questions.question: The cold weather season (winter) in India lasts during which months?
questions.explanation: Winter in India is from December to February. March to May is the hot weather season and June to September is the rainy season.

questions.question: The south-west monsoon winds bring rain to India because they blow from:
questions.explanation: These winds blow from the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal towards the land, so they carry a lot of moisture. Winds blowing from land to sea are dry and give little rain.

questions.question: Which of the following regions of India receives very little rainfall?
questions.explanation: Western Rajasthan has the Thar Desert and gets very little rain. The Kerala coast, Meghalaya and the Assam valley are among the rainiest parts of India.

questions.question: Which mountain range protects India from the bitterly cold winds of Central Asia?
questions.explanation: The high Himalayas stand like a wall in the north and stop the cold winds from Central Asia. The Aravallis, Western Ghats and Vindhyas lie inside India and are much lower.

questions.question: In which months does the monsoon retreat (go back) from India?
questions.explanation: October and November form the season of the retreating monsoon, when the rain-bearing winds move back towards the sea. July and August are the peak rainy months, not the retreat.
